question: Does opening a recording cost one container open, and stay the same project when it moves?

versions.ffmpeg: ffmpeg version 2025-02-06-git-6da82b4485-full_build-www.gyan.dev Copyright (c) 2000-2025 the FFmpeg developers

notes: footage is generated: tiny clips encoded on the spot, so this does not depend on what is in video-tests/
RUN WITH --broken: a project trusts whatever its document last recorded without checking the file against it. `carry` is expected to FAIL.
headers: '128×96 · 2s · h264'; a half-copied file was refused rather than becoming an empty project
derived: tmptcdctcav/cache-elsewhere and .sieve/take-02 — named for the recording, so a folder of footage cannot collide
identity: a recording renamed on disk is one row, under the id in its own document
library: 2 rows, newest first, a missing recording kept and marked, forgetting a row leaving the file alone
carry: an unchanged recording costs a stat, and a re-exported one is read again rather than served at the shape it used to be
bulk: 5 opened and 2 handed back in one gesture — one unreadable file is not a reason for the rest to fail
adopt (a document, and one identity): 2 checked, 0 disagreed
library (a list, not a filesystem): 3 checked, 0 disagreed
carry (fingerprint, not a re-read): 2 checked, 2 disagreed; first: a changed recording was not re-read
